full_text:
IMD issues an orange alert for five southern Odisha districts as Cyclone Murasu moves toward Andhra Pradesh, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds
OdishaPlus Bureau
Southern Odisha is bracing for another spell of heavy rainfall as Cyclone Murasu is expected to influence weather conditions across the state over the next few days, even as several districts continue to recover from the impact of Cyclone Arnab.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange warning for Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 3 and 4.
Although the system is not expected to make a direct landfall in Odisha, its movement towards the south Andhra Pradesh coast is likely to trigger widespread rainfall, thunderstorms and gusty winds in several parts of the state.
According to the IMD forecast, the system is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal before crossing the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narasapur by the morning of November 3. Wind speeds during landfall are expected to reach 100-110 kmph, with gusts up to 120 kmph.
Weather activity in Odisha is likely to increase from Sunday, with several places expected to receive light to moderate rain accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. A yellow warning has been issued for thunderstorms and rainfall in 16 districts.
On November 2, southern Odisha is likely to experience light to moderate rainfall, with heavy showers of 7-12 cm expected at isolated places in Ganjam and Gajapati. Thunderstorms and lightning are also likely in several coastal and southern districts.
The situation is expected to intensify on November 3 and 4. Besides the five districts under orange warning, isolated heavy rainfall is forecast in Nabarangpur, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Nayagada, Khordha and Puri on November 3.
On November 4, heavy rainfall is likely to continue in the five southern districts, while Nuapada, Nayagada, Puri, Khordha, Bolangir and Baragada may also receive heavy showers.
The IMD has advised people to follow weather bulletins, take shelter during thunderstorms to avoid lightning strikes and comply with traffic advisories in urban areas.
Rainfall activity is expected to gradually decline from November 5, although isolated places may continue to experience light to moderate showers and thunderstorms. Conditions are likely to improve considerably on November 6 and 7.
The latest weather development has put southern Odisha on alert, particularly after the recent flooding and disruption caused by Cyclone Arnab. The possibility of another spell of heavy rainfall has raised concerns over waterlogging, localised flooding and the difficulties of restoring normalcy in already affected areas.

full_text:
Chennai and Tiruvallur have been placed under an orange alert for extremely heavy rainfall as a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, according to a bulletin issued by the Chennai weather centre on November 2.
The storm was centred about 160 kilometres southeast of Nellore and 180 kilometres northeast of Chennai when the bulletin was issued. It was moving west-northwest and could cross the coast between Nellore and Narasapur from late on November 2 into the early hours of November 3, the weather centre said.
Winds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour could accompany the system during landfall, according to the bulletin. The combination of intense rainfall and strong winds could affect travel, public services and exposed urban areas in Chennai and Tiruvallur, where the orange alert applies for November 2.
An orange alert indicates the possibility of extremely heavy rainfall and requires authorities and residents to remain prepared for significant weather impacts. In the Chennai metropolitan region, heavy rain can place pressure on roads, drainage networks and other essential urban systems, although the weather bulletin supplied for this report does not provide a forecast of specific local flooding or infrastructure damage.
The bulletin also identified districts under yellow alerts for heavy rainfall on later dates. The Nilgiris may receive heavy rain on November 3, while Dindigul and Theni may receive heavy rain on November 5. The report refers to yellow alerts covering five districts, but the supplied bulletin does not specify the remaining district names or provide further details for the dates of November 6 and 7.
The storm’s projected track places the immediate focus on coastal Andhra Pradesh, while Chennai and Tiruvallur remain within the area forecast for extremely heavy rain. The weather centre’s advisory provides the current location, movement and expected landfall window, but does not state whether schools, public transport services or government offices will be closed.
The next operational milestone is the storm’s expected coastal crossing between Nellore and Narasapur from late November 2 to early November 3. Further changes to rainfall alerts, wind conditions and district-level precautions will depend on subsequent updates from the weather authorities.
